result.topic_en: Calculation introducing two functions y and y_1 defined via the square root of a derivative, their transformation under a linear substitution with determinant ad-bc, and the Wronskian-type relations they satisfy, leading to the common second-order linear differential equation.
result.transcription:
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{\partial z}{\partial g}}} = y \qquad \frac{z}{\sqrt{\frac{\partial z}{\partial g}}} = y_1$
$y \mp c y + d y_1 \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{ad-bc}}$
$y_1 \mp a y + b y_1 \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{ad-bc}}$
$y \frac{\partial y_1}{\partial g} - y_1 \frac{\partial y}{\partial g} = 1$
$y \frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial g^2} - y_1 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial g^2} = 0$
$\frac{1}{y} \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial g^2} = \frac{1}{y_1} \frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial g^2}$

methods.what: Definition of two functions from z(g) via inverse square root of the derivative
methods.quote: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{\partial z}{\partial g}}} = y \qquad \frac{z}{\sqrt{\frac{\partial z}{\partial g}}} = y_1$

methods.what: Transformation of (y, y_1) under a linear fractional substitution of z, normalised by 1/sqrt(ad-bc)
Wronskian of y and y_1 equals 1
Differentiating the constant Wronskian gives vanishing of y y_1'' - y_1 y''
Hence y and y_1 satisfy the same equation y''/y = invariant (Schwarzian-type second-order linear ODE)
